description: The configuration surface of the kube-ovn-vpc-peering chart. GENERATED from values.yaml by `./build.sh Charts` and diffed in CI — docs/plan/03 § charts/. Edit values.yaml, never this file. Members carrying `x-cybercloud-api: false` are chart or platform plumbing and are not part of the resource body.

link.description: The point-to-point range the two routers address each other on.

v4.description: A small IPv4 range, /30 or wider, that is in neither network. This network's peer port takes its first host address and the remote's takes the second. ⚠ It is checked against the platform's reserved ranges like any other, so link-local space cannot be used.

localAddressSpace.description: The range this network advertises to the remote — the remote's router gets one static route to it.

v4.description: This network's IPv4 range, in CIDR form — normally its address space. ⚠ It may not overlap the remote range or the link, and the refusal names both.

nameOverride.description: Replace the generated object-name stem. Empty means derive it from the release name.
nameOverride.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Helm plumbing. Nothing about it belongs in a resource body.

platform.description: Resource identity injected by the reconciler. Not a tenant-facing setting.

apiVersion.description: The api-version the resource was last written at. Not rendered, for the labels' reason.
apiVersion.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

localConnectIP.description: The link's first host address with the link's prefix — the local peer port's `localConnectIP`, and the remote route's `nextHopIP` without the prefix.
localConnectIP.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

localVpc.description: The local network's Vpc object name — VirtualNetworks.ObjectNameOf(namespace, the parent network read off the ADDRESS). The remote's fragment names it as `remoteVpc`.
localVpc.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

managedBy.description: Value of the cybercloud.io/managed-by label the co-owned apply requires on BOTH live objects before it writes.
managedBy.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

remoteConnectIP.description: The link's second host address with the link's prefix — the remote peer port's `localConnectIP`, and the local route's `nextHopIP` without the prefix.
remoteConnectIP.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

remoteVpc.description: The remote network's Vpc object name — VirtualNetworks.ObjectNameOf(namespace, the tenant's `remoteNetwork` value). ⚠ Qualified with THIS resource's namespace, which is what keeps a body inside its own resource group. The local fragment names it as `remoteVpc`.
remoteVpc.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceGroup.description: Resource group name. Not rendered, for the same reason.
resourceGroup.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceId.description: Resource GUID. Keys the three per-fragment annotations the builder writes on each Vpc — cybercloud.io/fragment.{resourceId}, fragment-hash.{resourceId}, fragment-path.{resourceId}.
resourceId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceType.description: Fully qualified resource type. Not rendered as a label; recorded here so the surface says what it is the surface of.
resourceType.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

subscriptionId.description: Subscription GUID. Not rendered — the labels on both Vpcs are their owners'.
subscriptionId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

tenantId.description: Tenant GUID. ⚠ On this type it is CHECKED rather than rendered: a co-writer writes no labels, and the co-owned apply refuses an object whose cybercloud.io/tenant-id is not this one.
tenantId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

platform.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

remoteAddressSpace.description: The range the remote advertises to this network — this network's router gets one static route to it.

v4.description: The remote network's IPv4 range, in CIDR form — normally its address space. ⚠ Two networks with overlapping ranges cannot be peered, which is the one place this platform's 'overlapping your own networks is fine' stops applying: a route to a range you also hold has nowhere to go.

remoteNetwork.description: The name of the virtualNetworks resource in the same resource group to peer this network with. ⚠ A name, not a resource id: the remote must be in this subscription and resource group, and a network in another cannot be named — write on the peering has to imply write on both networks. A remote that does not exist keeps the peering in progress until it does. Cannot be changed once created; delete the peering and create another.
